scientific_question: Does causal daily competitive capital allocation improve portable compounded wealth and/or drawdown versus fixed-horizon holding when capital is limited?

choices: replace incumbent with materially better eligible challenger
architecture.principle: Each capital slot is awarded to the best causally justified use today; elapsed holding time is not a predictor or exit rule.
architecture.replacement_hurdle: challenger must exceed incumbent by a frozen evidence margin sufficient for execution friction and estimation uncertainty; no switching merely for a trivial rank change
architecture.safe_asset: FRED DGS3MO, causal forward-filled only after observation, accrued ACT/365
architecture.regime_rule: market regime and security position are separate; regime authority is reevaluated daily; no position may carry a prior regime's authority through a fixed clock

execution.equity_friction: model spread/slippage and applicable regulatory friction separately; do not invent a broker commission
execution.shorts: borrow availability/fee limitation must be reported separately
execution.options: excluded from this first equity allocation comparison
execution.decision_timing: signals/predictors known by close t may affect execution no earlier than next session open

evidence_sequence.subsequent_test: TEST17, explicitly consumed/subsequent test and not pristine blind
evidence_sequence.rule: freeze complete policy and advancement gate before preserved50; no redesign after preserved50 or TEST17 reveal

comparison.control: existing fixed-horizon architecture using its already-frozen rules
diagnostics: reason for each exit: deterioration vs replacement vs regime transition
days actually held as an outcome, never a rule

development_validation.cross_sectional: deterministic 5-fold DEV50 stock holdout during selection
development_validation.temporal: era/year transport where data support it
development_validation.anti_leakage: no future outcomes, future peaks/troughs, future regime identity, ticker identity, or elapsed holding horizon as predictive features
development_validation.selection_unit: portfolio/date economics, not raw trade count

advancement_gate.principle: dynamic allocator must show portable economic improvement, not merely higher turnover or one lucky cohort
must_pass: positive DEV50 out-of-fold aggregate incremental terminal wealth versus fixed-horizon control after modeled friction
no worse DEV50 out-of-fold exact daily MTM max drawdown by more than 10% relative unless CAGR improvement is at least 20% relative
positive incremental result in at least 4 of 5 stock folds
positive incremental result across at least 60% of evaluated years/eras
no single ticker contributes more than 15% of total positive incremental PnL
advancement_gate.preserved50_gate: same directional thesis must remain positive on preserved50 without parameter change before TEST17 is opened

notes: Earlier 3/5/10/20-day Defensive experiment is diagnostic only for this question; its universal 20-session boundary selection is treated as evidence that the fixed horizon may be constraining/contaminating the solution.
Do not use post-trough NORMAL returns to validate a DEFENSIVE position merely because a fixed holding clock remains open.
Natural holding duration is measured after the fact.

regime_governance.state_path: NORMAL -> A/B/C crash detection -> DEFENSIVE -> recovery evidence -> R1 -> NORMAL
regime_governance.separation: Market-state controller determines permitted risk/exposure/action set. Daily allocator chooses among permitted uses of capital only.
regime_governance.defensive_rule: When A/B/C declares DEFENSIVE, daily allocation remains constrained by the frozen Defensive mechanisms; attractive security-level signals cannot silently restore NORMAL exposure.
defensive_controls: reduced/limited risky exposure as defined by validated Defensive policy
daily reassessment and immediate handoff when recovery/R1 state becomes authoritative
prohibitions: daily allocator may not infer R1/NORMAL from a profitable security
security profitability may not override A/B/C DEFENSIVE state
no fixed holding clock may carry a DEFENSIVE position beyond regime authority
regime_governance.normal_rule: NORMAL also uses daily competitive allocation rather than a fixed holding clock, subject to NORMAL exposure/risk rules.
regime_governance.r1_rule: R1 controls permitted exposure during recovery; daily allocation remains subordinate to R1 limits.

amendment.reason: Explicitly preserve crash-market Defensive activity limits before any outcome run.
